summary: Tinidazole is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial for trichomoniasis, giardiasis, amebiasis (intestinal and amebic liver abscess) and bacterial vaginosis. It is structurally related to metronidazole and carries a BOXED WARNING about potential carcinogenicity based on metronidazole rodent data - use is limited to approved indications and chronic use is avoided. Most indications use a single 2 g dose or a short 2 g/day course, taken with food. Avoid alcohol during and for 3 days after therapy.
indications: Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis) - treat sexual partners simultaneously
Giardiasis (Giardia duodenalis) in patients aged 3 years and older
Amebiasis - intestinal disease and amebic liver abscess (age 3 and older)

dosage.d: Single 2 g oral dose with food; treat partner simultaneously
dosage.n: Re-treatment with same dose if needed

dosage.d: Adults: single 2 g with food. Children >3 yr: single 50 mg/kg (up to 2 g) with food
Adults: 2 g/day for 3 days. Children >3 yr: 50 mg/kg/day (up to 2 g/day) for 3 days, with food
Adults: 2 g/day for 3-5 days. Children >3 yr: 50 mg/kg/day (up to 2 g/day) for 3-5 days, with food
2 g once daily for 2 days, OR 1 g once daily for 5 days, with food

admin: Take with food to minimize epigastric discomfort and GI side effects
For trichomoniasis, treat sexual partners at the same time to prevent reinfection
For children unable to swallow tablets, the pharmacist can prepare an oral suspension from crushed tablets in cherry syrup (taken with food)
Avoid alcohol and propylene-glycol-containing products during therapy and for 3 days afterward
Complete the prescribed course; limit to approved indications and avoid chronic use
moa: Tinidazole is a nitroimidazole. After entering susceptible organisms, its nitro group is reduced by anaerobic/microaerophilic metabolism to reactive intermediates that damage microbial DNA, inhibiting synthesis and causing cell death of susceptible protozoa and anaerobic bacteria.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to tinidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives (reactions range from urticaria to Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
Cockayne syndrome (risk of severe, irreversible hepatotoxicity reported with related nitroimidazoles)
monitor: CBC with repeated courses or in patients with blood dyscrasias

preg: Avoid in the first trimester (contraindicated). Data later in pregnancy are limited; use only if clearly needed, weighing the risks of untreated genital tract infection. The structurally related metronidazole is generally preferred when a nitroimidazole is required in pregnancy.
lact: Tinidazole passes into breast milk. Withhold breastfeeding during therapy and for 3 days after the last dose.
renal: Tinidazole is removed by hemodialysis - give a supplemental dose (e.g., one-half the usual dose) after dialysis when a scheduled dose coincides with a session. No major adjustment for moderate renal impairment alone.
hepatic: Metabolized hepatically; use with caution and consider dose reduction with monitoring in significant hepatic impairment, as clearance is reduced.

major: Alcohol / propylene glycol - disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia); avoid during and 3 days after
Disulfiram - psychotic reactions reported; avoid within 2 weeks
Warfarin and other oral anticoagulants - potentiated anticoagulant effect; monitor INR
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenobarbital, phenytoin) - reduce tinidazole levels
CYP3A4 inhibitors (cimetidine, ketoconazole) - increase tinidazole levels
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; food does not affect overall absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol during therapy and for at least 3 days after the last dose (disulfiram-like reaction).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient leukopenia/neutropenia on CBC; may transiently affect liver enzymes.

monitoring: Clinical resolution of infection (and partner treatment in trichomoniasis)
CBC with repeated courses or in patients with blood dyscrasias
Neurologic status - discontinue if abnormal neurologic signs (neuropathy/seizures) develop
counsel: Take with food to reduce stomach upset and finish the full course
Do NOT drink alcohol during treatment and for 3 days after - it can cause flushing, nausea and vomiting
A metallic taste is common and harmless
For trichomoniasis, your sexual partner should be treated at the same time and avoid intercourse until both are treated
Stop and seek care if you develop numbness/tingling, seizures, severe rash or signs of an allergic reaction
pk: Rapid and complete oral absorption; acts within hours
Cmax ~1.6 h after a 2 g dose
Long half-life allows single-dose or once-daily therapy
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNING: potential carcinogenicity (based on metronidazole rodent data) - limit to approved indications and avoid chronic use
Single 2 g dose cures most trichomoniasis and giardiasis - treat partners for trichomoniasis
Strict alcohol avoidance during and 3 days after (disulfiram-like reaction)
Contraindicated in the first trimester and in Cockayne syndrome
Longer half-life and often better tolerated than metronidazole, allowing shorter courses
missed: For multi-day courses, take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the schedule - do not double up. Single-dose regimens generally do not need a make-up dose.
overdose: There are no specific overdose reports or a specific antidote. Manage with supportive care and gastric lavage if appropriate; tinidazole is dialyzable, so hemodialysis can hasten removal in significant overdose.
